chunks: He ordered him to break his self from desires, and to restrain it at the time of its galloping (excess), for the self is a commander of evil, except what Allah has mercy.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali advise regarding the control of desires in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructs Malik al-Ashtar to engage in rigorous self-discipline, specifically commanding him to break the soul's dominance over desires and curb its unruly impulses. This advice builds upon the Quranic premise that the soul is inherently prone to evil, emphasizing that divine mercy is the necessary counterbalance to this natural inclination. The instruction highlights the practical application of spiritual purification for leaders, ensuring that personal appetites do not corrupt public governance.
